newsitem.title: USA: San Diego to sell solid waste system for $184 mln.
newsitem.headline: San Diego to sell solid waste system for $184 mln.

text.p: San Diego County's chief administrator recommended on Wednesday that the county sell its solid waste system to Allied Waste Industries Inc for $184 million.
Chief Administrative Officer Lawrence Prior tapped Allied Waste's bid over competing offers by USA Waste Services Inc and Waste Management Inc, county spokeswoman Carol Conner said.
The county Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote on the contract on August 12. Once approved by the board, the sale should close in November, Conner said.

Under the contract, Allied Waste will take over the county's solid waste system, which includes four landfills, a transfer station, a recycling plant and all county-owned and leased waste bin and container sites.
The company also would assume the system's future environmental liabilities.
The privatization of a municipal asset of this size is unprecedented in California.
The money will be used by San Diego County to establish an environmental trust fund for the maintenance of inactive landfills and to build up the county budget reserve.
